### Problem: Plus One {#sec-arr-p4-a}

::: {.p-statement}
Given a non-negative integer as a list of digits, most significant first ($1 \le n \le 100$, each digit $0$–$9$, no leading zeros), return the digits of that integer plus one. Example: $[1, 2, 3] \to [1, 2, 4]$, $[9, 9, 9] \to [1, 0, 0, 0]$.

Source: [LC 66 · Plus One](https://leetcode.com/problems/plus-one/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
It is grade-school addition with a carry. Start at the **least** significant digit (the right end): add the carry, write the remainder, pass on the tens. Only when every digit was a $9$ do you gain a new leading `1`.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Naive.** Join into an integer, add 1, split back. In Python this works (integers are unbounded) but builds a $100$-digit number; in C++ or Java it overflows as soon as the number has more than about $18$ digits.
2. **Simulate the carry right-to-left.** `carry = 1`; for `i` from the last index down, `d = a[i] + carry`, store `d % 10`, new `carry = d // 10`; stop early when the carry dies. If a carry remains, prepend `1`.

**Invariant.** After handling positions $i{+}1..n-1$, those cells hold the final digits of the result there, and `carry` is what must still be added at position $i$. The carry is only ever $0$ or $1$, and it survives a digit only if that digit was a $9$, which is why the loop can stop at the first digit that is not a $9$.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Convert to an integer, add, split back

::: {.form-next}
Join the digits into a number, add one, and split it back into digits. It reads exactly like the problem, and Python's unbounded integers make it correct, so it serves as the brute force below. In C++ a `long long` holds only 18 full digits and the input may have $100$, so this form is only a check for short inputs there.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def plus_one_brute(digits):
    num = 0
    for d in digits:
        num = num * 10 + d
    num += 1
    return [int(c) for c in str(num)]
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
#include <string>
using namespace std;

vector<int> plusOneBrute(vector<int>& digits) {   // only valid while the value fits
    long long num = 0;
    for (int d : digits) num = num * 10 + d;
    ++num;
    vector<int> out;
    for (char c : to_string(num)) out.push_back(c - '0');
    return out;
}
```
:::

#### Propagate the carry right-to-left

::: {.form-next}
Grade-school addition with a carry. Start at the least significant digit: `carry = 1`, write `d % 10`, pass on `d // 10`, and stop the instant the carry dies. Only an all-nines input carries out of the front and gains a new leading `1`. $O(n)$ worst case, $O(1)$ beyond the output.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("plusone", "carry")
    assert str(final) == "[1, 0, 0, 0]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arr-plus-one
def plus_one(digits: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    a = list(digits)
    i = len(a) - 1
    carry = 1
    while i >= 0 and carry:
        s = a[i] + carry
        a[i] = s % 10
        carry = s // 10
        i -= 1
    if carry:
        a = [1] + a
    return a


for _ in range(1500):
    d = [random.randint(0, 9) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 8))]
    if len(d) > 1:
        d[0] = random.randint(1, 9)          # no leading zero
    assert plus_one(d) == plus_one_brute(d)

assert plus_one([1, 2, 3]) == [1, 2, 4]
assert plus_one([9]) == [1, 0]
assert plus_one([9, 9, 9]) == [1, 0, 0, 0]    # the board sample
print("plus_one OK")
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
using namespace std;

vector<int> plusOne(vector<int>& digits) {
    int carry = 1;
    for (int i = (int)digits.size() - 1; i >= 0 && carry; --i) {
        int s = digits[i] + carry;
        digits[i] = s % 10;
        carry = s / 10;
    }
    if (carry) digits.insert(digits.begin(), 1);
    return digits;
}
```
:::
:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Convert to an integer, add, split back** is $O(n)$ arithmetic steps in Python (on big integers) but overflows a fixed-width type once the number has more than about 18 digits, which $n \le 100$ allows. **Propagate the carry right-to-left** is $O(n)$ worst case (all nines), $O(1)$ the moment the carry stops, and $O(1)$ space beyond the output (the new leading digit appears only in the all-nines case).
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- All nines: length grows by one, e.g. $[9,9]\to[1,0,0]$.
- Trailing digit below $9$: carry dies after one step.
- The number $0$ itself, if the judge passes it: $[0]\to[1]$.
- Inserting the new leading `1` at the front costs $O(n)$, but it happens at most once, and only for all nines; storing digits least significant first would turn it into a `push_back`.
:::
